_comment: Terms for the lesson propaganda-public-opinion. status: ok = attested in a Turkish source I opened; chosen = my own rendering; check = weakly attested, needs a Turkish-language reviewer. Existing keys (public-opinion, pseudo-environment, opinion-leader, propaganda-model, informed-consent) are NOT redefined here; notes on how they are used in this lesson are attached to new keys.

pseudo-environment-alt.note: The lesson uses the course-wide ‘sözde çevre’ (see agenda-setting terminology). A bookseller’s description of the 2020 Turkish edition of Public Opinion (Kabalcı; kitapyurdu.com and idefix.com repeat one blurb) lists ‘Stereotip’, ‘Sahte Çevre’ and ‘Sahte Gerçek’; no scholarly Turkish source using ‘sahte çevre’ was opened.

stereotype.note: ‘Stereotip’ is in the Turkish edition blurb (see above). ‘Kalıp yargı’ is offered from my own knowledge of usage as an alternative and was not confirmed in a source I opened.

manufacture-of-consent.note: ‘Rızanın İmalatı’ is the Turkish title of Herman & Chomsky’s Manufacturing Consent as it appears in the title of Gadimov 2015 (İlef Dergisi 2(2), 215-226) and in several Turkish book listings (translator Ender Abadoğlu; publishers and years differ across listings, not used). ‘Rıza üretimi’ occurred only in a search snippet (a thesis title beginning ‘Toplumsal Rıza Üretiminde …’) and is treated as unconfirmed.

engineering-of-consent.note: My own rendering of Bernays’s 1947 phrase; no Turkish source was opened for it.

phantom-public.note: No Turkish rendering of Lippmann’s 1925 title was found (web searches returned none). ‘Kamu’ for ‘the public’ follows the existing Dewey person file (‘kamu tutulma içinde’). Own translation.

lippmann-dewey-debate.note: The Turkish website journo.com.tr published a translation of notes by Carl R. Bybee titled ‘Gazeteciliğin demokrasi için önemi: Lippmann ve Dewey’nin “kamuoyu” tartışması’ (17 July 2022); a web-page summary, not a scholarly source.

propagandist-technician.note: The lesson’s own shorthand, not Lasswell’s term. ‘Propagandacı’ is in the TDK dictionary (‘Propaganda yapan kimse; propagandist’).

omnicompetent-citizen.note: Lippmann’s ‘omnicompetent citizen’ (Public Opinion, chapter XVII and elsewhere; Dewey 1927 quotes it as ‘omni-competent’). No Turkish source opened; own rendering.

organized-intelligence.note: Title of Part VIII of Public Opinion. ‘İstihbarat’ (intelligence in the sense of intelligence bureau) is my own choice; ‘örgütlü bilgi/zekâ’ would be another option. No Turkish source opened.

outsider-insider.note: Lippmann’s outsider and insider are positions, not social types (Schudson 2008). Own rendering; the lesson keeps the English ‘outsider’ in one quotation.

public-opinions-capital.en: public opinions vs Public Opinion (capital letters)
public-opinions-capital.note: Lippmann’s distinction between individuals’ ‘public opinions’ and ‘Public Opinion with capital letters’ has no ready Turkish equivalent because ‘kamuoyu’ is a collective singular (TDK: ‘bir konuyla ilgili halkın genel düşüncesi’). Own solution.

kanaat.note: TDK Güncel Türkçe Sözlük: 4 senses, the first ‘elindekinden hoşnut olma’, the fourth ‘görüş’. The course already uses ‘kanaat önderi’ (opinion leader) and Kutlu 2019 uses ‘kanaat iklimi’.

riza.note: TDK: ‘Razı olma, bir şeyi yapmayı isteme; onam’. The course’s research-methods terminology uses ‘onam’ for ‘informed consent’.

significant-symbols.note: From Lasswell 1927: ‘the control of opinion by significant symbols’. Own rendering.

intelligence-bureau.note: Lippmann’s proposal in chapters XXV–XXVIII. Own rendering.
